newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-BASF Magnetics sees few job losses after sale.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-BASF Magnetics sees few job losses after sale.

text.p: German BASF Magnetics said on Wednesday no drastic job losses were likely after South Korean textile group Kohap Ltd takes over the worldwide tape business from January 1, 1997.
"From today's perspective I don't expect any drastic personnel measures to hit us," said Juergen Langeheine, chairman of BASF Magnetics.
Langeheine said he thought the company, which posted sales of 1.5 billion marks ($985.2 million) last year and employs 3,700 workers, could show marginally positive profits for 1996.
BASF said on Tuesday it had sold its Magnetics subsidiary for an undisclosed sum to Kohap.
"We expect that all positions will be maintained, as long as the business stays in the black," said BASF board member Max Dietrich Kley.
The sale to the Kohap Ltd came as a surprise after BASF this summer signed a letter of understanding with RAKS Holding AS leaving the Turkish group the likely new owner.
RAKS on Wednesday accused BASF of having broken the terms of the two groups' understanding.
"BASF did not conform to the terms of the agreement," RAKS said in a statement.

After the statement of understanding had been signed some members of BASF's supervisory board had expressed doubt as to whether RAKS, posting sales of 400 million marks, would be able to manage Magnetics, industry sources said.
BASF itself has never issued any comment expressing any doubt about RAKS' competence.

Magnetics, which has absorbed 600 million marks in subsidies from BASF in the last five years, had previously said it expected to post a 1996 operating loss of around 20 million marks, as a result of heavy price competiton.
Kohap board member S.K. Bang said Magnetics, which is one of the world's best known tape brands, should remain an independent business area within the Kohap group.
"If the company makes profits and goes in the right direction, why should we change it," said Bang.
Kohap, which is South Korea's leading integrated producer of synthetic fabrics and yarns, will take over the BASF magnetic tape production plants at Ludwigshafen, Willstaett und Munich.
BASF had long been trying to sell the loss-making Magnetics group to concentrate on its core chemical, drug and agricultural business.
